forecaster_note: Sat: S swell easing but still a fun chest- to head-high set at the S-facing magnets; light N winds add texture, NE picks up into midday so N corners/S-facing spots are the call — go early at the smaller S corners. Sun: S leftovers + short-period NE wind wave, waist–chest, cleanish early with offshores. — Surfline forecaster Max Stanley-Jones, Sat 31 Oct

wind.summary: Light N ~9 kph at dawn (offshore at Long Reef/Curl Curl), N 11 kph 9am; NE onshore 16 kph by noon, 25 kph (gusts 41) by 3pm. Sun dawn: W offshore 15 kph (gusts 45).

days.label: Today
days.note: S swell easing but still 192 kJ avg 6–12 (peak 246; 13s S easing + NE wind wave) — fun chest-high at S magnets, smaller at Dee Why. Light N dawn, NE onshore from midday: surf 6–10am, low 6:04am pushing to the 12:42pm high.
days.surfline_text: The S swell is easing back but there's still a fun enough chest to head high set across the Sth facing magnets. Light N winds are adding texture to most stretches. It'll be a day for the Nth corners as we're set to see this winds pick up into midday.   If you're going for the smaller Sth corner breaks, head for the early as later on they'll be looking even more junky and wind affected.

tip.label: Frontside Point
tip.text: Dead S swell wraps poorly here — Point rights frontside, expect the small end. Light N cross-shore at dawn; find a bank at the S end of the beach and get in before the 12:42pm high turns it NE-onshore.

tip.text: Southern corner by the wall catches most of the S swell; the rest is peaky. Cleanish early, junky once NE arrives.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: 88 kJ avg (peak 111) — small NE wind wave 7s + weak S. Smaller, peaky waist–chest from S leftovers + NE wind wave. Offshore W at dawn, cleanish early, onshore SE/E by midday — early only.
days.surfline_text: S swell leftovers mixed with short period NE wind wave - about waist to chest high, depending on exposure.  Cleanish in the morning with offshore winds looking likely. Then light onshores through the mid-morning and still OK. Lumpier and bumpier into the afternoon as onshores pick up more.
